ReviewProbe.Head: 8a123f69bcc2333cc0d9e0ec41a05af400e75401
ReviewProbe.Scope: One independent read-only review of exact QR BCH distance lookup, first-use initialization and thread safety, format-first timing tiebreak equivalence, complete semantic sampling extraction, framework boundaries and contract-focused tests.
ReviewProbe.ProductApiDisposition: Accept as shaped: work remains in the existing QR engine, no new public API or runtime dependency; semantic partials improve maintainability.
ReviewProbe.IndependentEvidence: Compared all 53 original and candidate members including attributes. All are text-identical except precisely the comment and two guards in FindBestPhase. Independently compared all 96 refinement vectors including output bit patterns.
Limits: Static inspection; full framework qualification and frozen corpus runs remain primary-owned.
Exploratory paired scans are warmed and shared-host; multi-QR remains about one second and allocation increases.
The warmed timing lanes do not measure the cold first-use cost of the 32 KiB lookup. No first-scan latency advantage is claimed.
ReviewProbe.Publication: Local implementation only; no push, PR, external review, release or deployment.

ChangedDecoders: QR pixel refinement looks up the exact nearest BCH-format distance for both 15-bit observations in a shared 32 KiB table, initialized on first use from the canonical format-word generator. Full integer fallback remains for observations outside that domain. A strictly worse format score skips the timing tiebreaker; candidate order, equal-score ties, early exits, acceptance checks and recognition allowances remain unchanged.

The modern QR sampling implementation is split into refinement, interpolation, neighborhood, nine-point and twenty-five-point partials. Original method bodies and attributes are preserved, apart from the two timing-score guards. No public API or production dependency is added.
AttributionLimits: This follow-up records 195/267 correct positive images versus 195/267 in the previous pass. Previously correct images lost: none; gained: none. Paired negative completion is [30, 29, 30, 28]/31 with the current binary and [30, 30, 30, 29]/31 with the previous qualified binary. All outcomes remain sensitive to shared-host contention and wall-clock budgets; no universal timeout or recognition advantage is established. QR scoring reuses exact BCH distances and avoids timing work only when the primary format score cannot win. All candidate hypotheses and tie rules are preserved. Recognition budgets and search limits remain unchanged. Demonstrated regression gains do not establish accuracy on unseen photographs. Supplemental PDF417 images are regression evidence informed by prior remediation, not an unseen holdout. The invalid GS1 AI (3922) oracle and undeclared QR character encoding policies remain unchanged in scoring. Expanded Stacked multiple-symbol localization and arbitrary perspective remain unproved; MaxiCode image scanning is unsupported. The upstream RSS-14 group is recorded under Gs1DataBarOmnidirectional and includes stacked layouts: rss14-1/2.png and rss14-1/5.png are confirmed examples. CodeGlyphX has stacked DataBar module decoders but no stacked DataBar image scanner; those misses remain counted in the broader family coverage.

RegressionProof.Coverage: Every 15-bit observation and a permutation of paired observations are checked against independently constructed BCH words. Full integer boundary combinations protect fallback behavior. Ninety-six differential refinement vectors retain bit-identical outputs across global, hybrid and adaptive thresholds, dimensions 21 through 177 and both polarities. Existing QR perspective, rotated-image, photograph, parity, multi-symbol and budget contracts remain covered by the full suites.
RegressionProof.HistoricalProof: Earlier decoding qualification remains historical in previous-qualification.json and its retained archive. Current full suites and frozen/supplemental outcomes are rerun.

TestExecution.Net472: Task-local runner configuration disables collection parallelism; recognition allowances and assertions are unchanged.
TestExecution.Limit: Short wall-clock allowances remain sensitive to shared-host load. Serial legacy qualification is not proof for default parallel execution.

SupplementalPdf417.Selection: All PNG images with UTF-8 text oracles in pdf417-1, pdf417-2 and pdf417-3, excluding the 18 frozen comparison images. The 38-image selection was fixed before the first supplemental outcomes. One revealed regression informed the final correction and permanent fixture; the final set is supplemental regression evidence, not an unseen holdout.
SupplementalPdf417.Limit: Supplemental images from the same upstream collection, outside the 18 frozen comparison images. The initial check exposed a sampling-priority regression that was repaired and added to permanent tests. This is regression evidence used during remediation, not an unseen holdout for the final candidate, a replacement ranking, or proof on an independent dataset. Wall-clock budgets also limit attribution of changed outcomes.

DataBarStackedDiscovery.PublicNote: The RSS-14 corpus group includes single-row and stacked symbols. CodeGlyphX currently lacks stacked DataBar image recognition; those layout misses remain counted in the group result.
DataBarStackedDiscovery.Evidence: Both original unmodified images visibly contain two bar rows separated by a patterned separator. DataBar14Decoder exposes stacked and stacked-omnidirectional module decoders; SymbolCapabilities marks those variants as standard module capabilities without image scanning. CorpusReaders maps the upstream RSS-14 family to Gs1DataBarOmnidirectional for CodeGlyphX and to the broader RSS_14/DataBar family for the other engines.
DataBarStackedDiscovery.Impact: The existing row groups broader RSS-14 samples under the Omni identifier. Some recorded misses reflect missing stacked image support rather than failure to detect a single-row Omni symbol. These remain valid coverage losses and do not change the locked IDs, hashes, oracle text or measured outcomes.
DataBarStackedDiscovery.Disposition: Within the authorized decoding/comparison goal: disclose the family/layout boundary in methodology, then add stacked DataBar image recognition in a subsequent coherent implementation round. No dependency or scoring relaxation is proposed.

HintScopeProof.Limit: Broader hints can change reported single-row variant identities; the comparison scores exact payload sets and these are unchanged on all twelve samples. This diagnostic uses the previous qualified binary; the DataBar implementation is unchanged in this round.

QrScoringDiagnostics.Scope: Public scanner checks with preloaded pixels, two warmups, six retained observations per image, original 1500 ms allowance, CCD0 affinity and normal priority. These sequential shared-host observations are diagnostics, not a fair engine ranking. Frozen corpus and rotated timing lanes remain authoritative.
